source_ref: Bayazit, Gonullu & Dogan (2022) PLOS ONE 17(11):e0275672, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0275672, Table 1 (article XML); data: Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/M0NJIQ clinical_self_efficacy_dataset.tab (CC0); data/CSE_Bayazit_2022.R
note: IRW item codes Item1..Item15 ARE the Dataverse file's own column names (data/CSE_Bayazit_2022.R keeps them; only ID->id and Term dropped); the .tab is a semicolon CSV with no variable or value labels, so no level-1 source exists. Table 1 of the paper (CC BY 4.0) prints all 15 items numbered 1-15 in the administered Turkish with the authors' own English in brackets, plus per-item Mean/SD/loadings; the response-to-reviewers (s002) confirms Table 1 originally read 'Item 1 ... Item 15' and the labels were replaced by the statements, so rows 1-15 = Item1..Item15. item_text = Turkish verbatim from the article XML, item_text_translated = the bracketed English from the same row (study_supplied, not machine translated). Response anchors: the paper states only that the scale is a 5-point Likert item 'from "strongly disagree" to "strongly agree"' (English, in describing Kang et al. 2019's scale); no Turkish anchor wording is published in the paper, its two supplements (s001 reviewer-annotated manuscript, s002 response to reviewers, zero anchor text) or the deposit (no labels). So resp 1/5 carry those English endpoint labels in option_text and 2-4 are blank; direction 1=disagree is the stated convention and consistent with Table 1 means reproducing on the raw data. The 'short informative paragraph' given as instructions (definition of self-efficacy, meaning of 'this course'/'clinical skill') is not published; instructions left blank. The live table keeps all 15 items, including Item11, which the paper dropped from its final 14-item scale. Rights: L-SES originates in Kang et al. 2019 PLOS ONE 14(1):e0209155 (CC BY 4.0); Turkish wording from the CC BY 4.0 Bayazit article; no fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution clause located -- silence, not a grant; no register row written. Mapping check (verify_CSE_Bayazit_2022.R): per-item mean/SD within 0.062 of Table 1 for all 15 (Table 1 appears to be the EFA half-sample, live = all 651); Hungarian assignment on (mean,SD) picks the identity 15/15; 3-factor minres/oblimin EFA puts 13/14 non-cross-loading items on their published factor (Item12 splits Cog .43/Psy .34 vs published Psy .45) and Item11 cross-loads (.35/.31/.21) as published. PARTIAL: near-ties 4/11/12, 8/9, 1/2/3 are not individually separated by the statistics; the tie is carried by the paper's explicit numbering.
public_note: Item wording is the administered Turkish with the authors' English; the response anchors are only published in English and only at the endpoints (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree), so options 2-4 carry no text and the Turkish anchor wording respondents saw is not available.

source_ref: Deposit: Pinheiro, Cunha, Rodrigues et al. (2023) 'Replication Data for: Work Context's Impact on Common Mental Disorders Among Brazilian University Teachers During COVID-19', Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/GMZUB5 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), single file tmcs_professores_es.tab (datafile 7077034); processing script data/pinheiro_2023_trwcas.R (writes both sibling tables). Study paper: Cunha, Pinheiro, Aguiar et al. (2026) 'Impacto do contexto de trabalho para transtornos mentais comuns entre professores universitarios', Revista Psicologia em Pesquisa 20:e44013, doi:10.34019/1982-1247.2026.v20.44013 (CC BY-NC 4.0; English-language galley https://periodicos.ufjf.br/index.php/psicologiaempesquisa/article/download/44013/30456). Item wording: WHO, Beusenberg & Orley, 'A User's Guide to the Self Reporting Questionnaire', WHO/MNH/PSF/94.8 (1994), p.3 'SRQ-20' list, https://iris.who.int/server/api/core/bitstreams/3f890c49-b056-4112-bd0e-2e386ff08a39/content (sha256 19f26393f5b6473d736b8e7fbb1af3205bf0d0c41edeb67905ba4df85db562c6, matches the rights register). Cached under itemtext/.cache/pinheiro_2023_srq/.
note: Item text (c) World Health Organization -- SRQ-20 English wording from WHO/MNH/PSF/94.8 p.3, read off the rendered page image (the PDF text layer is a noisy OCR) and transcribed verbatim, 20/20; options are the page's own 'yes/no'. RIGHTS: instrument_rights_register.csv row for the SRQ-20 is verdict=ship_with_note; applied, not re-derived. WHO's clause: 'This document is not a formal publication of the World Health Organization (WHO), and all rights are reserved by the Organization. The document may, however, be freely reviewed, abstracted, reproduced or translated, in part or in whole, but not for sale or for use in conjunction with commercial purposes.' It grants free non-commercial reproduction rather than reserving a right beyond that, per the register ruling (same as the AUDIT row); IRW is non-commercial. The CC BY-NC-SA deposit and CC BY-NC paper are not the source of the wording (the deposit has no text; the paper quotes one example only). LANGUAGE: administered in Brazilian Portuguese (the paper cites the Goncalves, Stein & Kapczinski 2008 Brazilian adaptation). FALLBACK taken: the deposit (one .tab; DDI variable labels are bare column names srq_1..srq_20, no value labels) and the paper (no supplement; prints one SRQ example in English, 'Have you been feeling sad lately?') carry no Portuguese item text, so the base fields hold WHO's English and the _translated columns are blank; language=Portuguese. MAPPING: the IRW code IS the deposit column name (script pivots srq_* columns by name, pattern 1), but nothing in the deposit or paper ties srq_N to a wording, so srq_N -> SRQ-20 item N is inferred from the instrument's fixed canonical numbering (mapping_basis=paper_order, used for canonical order). Checked against the data (verify_pinheiro_2023_srq.R, PARTIAL): near-synonym pairs are mutual nearest neighbours -- 18/20 tired r=0.634 (matrix max), 7/19 digestion/stomach r=0.543, 8/12 thinking/decisions r=0.486; block 9/11/13/15 takes each member's top-2 correlates; item 6 'nervous, tense or worried' has the highest endorsement (0.702). Does not separate order within those pairs/block. RESP: 1=yes, 0=no, per WHO scoring ('A score of 1 indicates that the symptom was present'); the summed score reproduces the paper's Table 2 exactly (M 6.46, SD 4.67, N 235; flipped would be 13.54). INSTRUCTIONS left blank: WHO recommends a standard introduction, but nothing shows this online survey used it; the paper says only that items were answered yes/no for the prior 30 days.
public_note: Item text is the World Health Organization's English SRQ-20 (WHO/MNH/PSF/94.8); respondents answered the Brazilian Portuguese adaptation, whose wording can differ -- e.g. the study paper renders item 9 as 'Have you been feeling sad lately?' where WHO's English reads 'Do you feel unhappy?'

note: mapping_basis=data_labels, derivation core model s3 pattern 1: data/spain_2025_tourism.do imports 3521_num.csv, renames columns from their quoted headers, lower-cases all names, and in Bookmark 2 loops gen item = the literal column name over gradoimpor1_1..gradoimpor1_5 -- the IRW item code IS the CIS column name GRADOIMPOR1_1..5, lower-cased.
